record.paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), find more counterexamples beyond the Werner-Holevo channel and small perturbations of it, and determine whether the counterexamples support or refute the conjecture that multiplicativity holds throughout 1 ≤ p ≤ 2.

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Find more counter-examples to (24). Do they suggest that the conjecture holds for 1 ≤ p ≤ 2?
Very recently (July, 2007), Winter [51] solved Problem 11 by showing the existence of counter-examples for all p> 2.
Hayden [21] showed that there exist counter-examples for 1 < p <2 and this was extended to p = 2 by Winter.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)	o\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_A)$ be a quantum channel, i.e. a completely positive trace-preserving linear map between matrix algebras. For $1\le p\le\infty$ define the maximal output $p$-norm of $\Phi$ by
$$
u_p(\Phi)\;=\;\sup_{ho}\, igl\|\Phi(ho) igr\|_p,$$
where the supremum is taken over all density operators $ho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\|X\|_p=(\mathrm{Tr}|X|^p)^{1/p}$ is the Schatten $p$-norm.

Given two channels $\Phi$ and $\Omega$, the multiplicativity property at parameter $p$ asserts that
$$
u_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)\;=\;
u_p(\Phi)\,
u_p(\Omega). \qquad (\ast)$$

The Werner–Holevo channel on $d	imes d$ matrices is the channel
$$W_d(ho)\;=\; rac{1}{d-1} igl(\mathrm{Tr}(ho)\,I-ho^{T} igr),$$
which, together with small perturbations of it, is known to violate $(\ast)$ for some range of $p>2$.

Problem. Exhibit additional pairs of quantum channels $(\Phi,\Omega)$ that violate $(\ast)$ beyond Werner–Holevo channels and small perturbations thereof. Determine whether such counterexamples can occur in the range $1\le p\le 2$, and in particular decide whether the conjecture
$$
u_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=
u_p(\Phi)\,
u_p(\Omega)\quad	ext{for all channels }\Phi,\Omega 	ext{ and all } 1\le p\le 2$$
holds or fails.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved in the negative: Hayden constructed counterexamples to multiplicativity for all $1<p<2$, Winter extended this to $p=2$ and to all $p>2$, and Hastings (2008) subsequently disproved the additivity (and hence the $p\to 1$ multiplicativity) conjecture, showing that multiplicativity of the maximal output $p$-norm fails throughout $p>1$.

status_evidence.title: Hayden — counterexamples to maximal p-norm multiplicativity for every p>1
status_evidence.snippet: We demonstrate the existence of counterexamples to the maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture for all p>1.

status_evidence.title: Hastings — Superadditivity of communication capacity using entangled inputs
status_evidence.snippet: Disproof of the additivity conjecture for the minimum output entropy, implying failure of multiplicativity at p→1.
status_evidence.claim: Multiplicativity fails for p near 1 as well.

status_evidence.title: Winter — counterexamples to multiplicativity (2007)
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples to maximal p-norm multiplicativity for all p>2 and at p=2.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples extended to p=2 and all p>2.
